22346363.reason: The safety analysis pools randomized, single-blind and open-label studies and therefore cannot supply an independent randomized-trial adverse-event comparison.
22346363.source_span: Safety measures included antihypertensive drug-treated subpopulations from these four and three additional single-blind and open-label PRM studies of up to 1 year (N[PRM] = 650; N[placebo] = 632).

18036082.reason: The source describes a low incidence and minor severity of adverse events but reports no arm counts or effect with confidence interval.
18036082.source_span: The incidence of adverse events was low and most side-effects were judged to be of minor severity.

12790159.reason: The source reports no significant side-effect difference across placebo and two melatonin doses without dose-specific counts or effect with confidence interval.
12790159.source_span: RESULTS: There were no significant differences in sleep EEG, the amount or subjective quality of sleep or side effects between the placebo, 0.3-mg melatonin or 1.0-mg melatonin treatments.

27559258.source_span: After 1, 7, 14 days, the patients were reviewed with the Athens insomnia scale oral questionnaire to document the subjective sleep quality.
27559258.reason: Sleep is measured only with the Athens Insomnia Scale (a questionnaire score, reported as percentage improvements); sleep-onset latency in minutes is not reported, and a scale score is never converted to minutes. The trial enrolled DSM-IV primary insomnia in cancer patients: it stays eligible, its SOL is absent.
